title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting, from the previous page 'Conjectures Lefschetz locales'. S = Spec A, with A an excellent strictly (henselian) local ring and f in m_A. X is a local scheme of dimension N, probably normal with an isolated singularity: the N=2 case, which cites Mumford, only makes sense if X is not regular. Y = V(f) is a hypersurface section and U = X - Y. A^i denotes the codimension-i Chow group of these local schemes, the analogue of the local class group when i=1. It carries a filtration 0 -> J^i -> A^i -> N^i -> 0, with J^i the 'continuous/Jacobian' part and N^i the 'Néron–Severi' quotient.

The previous page stated three conjectures:
(1) Vanishing above the middle: N^i(X) is finite (mod finite groups) for i >= N/2, and J^i(X)=0 for i >= (N+1)/2.
(2) Local Lefschetz for restriction to Y, separately on J and N:
- J^i(X) -> J^i(Y) is bijective for i <= (N-2)/2 and injective for i <= (N-1)/2, except for p-torsion.
- N^i(X) -> N^i(Y) is bijective for i <= (N-3)/2 and injective for i <= (N-2)/2.

This page does four things.
(a) It combines the J and N statements via 0->J->A->N->0. A^i(X) -> A^i(Y) is bijective for i <= (N-3)/2 and injective for i <= (N-2)/2. The critical cases are i = (N-2)/2, (N-1)/2, N/2, and for N specifically N^{(N-2)/2} and N^{(N-1)/2}.
(b) Statement (3), described as a consequence of (1) and (2), concerns the localization sequence A^i(Y) -> A^{i+1}(X) -> A^{i+1}(U) -> 0. It claims A^i(X) -> A^i(U) is an isomorphism mod finite groups, and an isomorphism for small i. Equivalently, the Gysin map A^i(Y) -> A^{i+1}(X) is zero mod finite groups, and zero for small i. The mechanism is i^* i_* = c_1(O(Y)|_Y) = 0 because Y is principal. So the image of the Gysin map lies in ker(A^{i+1}(X) -> A^{i+1}(Y)), which vanishes by (2) in low degree. Above the middle the target is finite by (1).
(c) Problem (4) has two parts. First, define 'intersection forms' N^i(X) x N^i(X) -> Z on these local groups. Second, define a 'theory of vanishing cycles' for algebraic cycles that explains the critical maps J^{(N-1)/2}(X) -> J^{(N-1)/2}(Y) and N^{(N-2)/2}(X) -> N^{(N-2)/2}(Y). This is a Picard–Lefschetz/SGA7-type picture transported to Chow groups of singularities.
(d) The example N=2 (normal surface singularity):
- (1) says N^1(X), the discrete part of the local class group, is finite. Grothendieck identifies this as Mumford's theorem (1961), the negative definiteness of the intersection matrix of the exceptional curves of a resolution, a local Hodge-index statement. The finite group is the discriminant group of that lattice.
- (2) and (3) are empty.
- The essential group is J^1(X), the continuous part of Cl (Pic^0 of a resolution, which is non-trivial for non-rational singularities).

The next page continues with N=3 and N=4. There Grothendieck asks for a natural complement of J^1(X) in J^1(Y) given by 'vanishing cycles', and for a reinterpretation of the Hodge index theorem as negativity of a form on N^1(X). The overall aim is a higher-codimension, Chow-theoretic generalization of the SGA2 local Lefschetz theorems for Pic and Cl (Grothendieck–Samuel parafactoriality), organized by the Milnor/Lefschetz pattern of degrees around the middle dimension.
errors: The two halves of (3) are equivalent by the exact localization sequence A^{i-1}(Y) -> A^i(X) -> A^i(U) -> 0. So the bound for 'A^i(X)->A^i(U) iso' (i <= (N-1)/2) should correspond to 'A^{i}(Y)->A^{i+1}(X) zero' for i <= (N-3)/2. Grothendieck writes the same bound (N-1)/2 for both, an off-by-one inconsistency.

The derivation 'from 1 and 2' via i^*i_* = 0 has a gap at the middle degree. It gives Gysin = 0 only when A^{i+1}(X)->A^{i+1}(Y) is injective, i.e. i+1 <= (N-2)/2. For N odd, the degree i+1 = (N-1)/2 is covered neither by (1) nor by injectivity on N^i, so the claimed isomorphism there is not a formal consequence. This is exactly a 'cas critique'.
The 'exc. p' (except p-torsion) qualifications of the previous page are silently dropped in the combined statements here.

Asking for Z-valued intersection forms on N^i(X) is problematic when N^i(X) is finite, as in the N=2 case, where it is the discriminant group of Mumford's lattice. The natural pairing on that finite group is Q/Z-valued: the linking form of the link, equivalently the discriminant form. A Z-valued negative definite form lives on the exceptional-divisor lattice of a resolution, not on N^1(X) itself.

The regularity hypothesis 'X, Y réguliers [?]' from the previous page is inconsistent with the N=2 example. A regular local X has A^1 = Cl = 0, which would make Mumford's theorem irrelevant. Normality or an isolated singularity must be intended.

ideas.what: Local Lefschetz conjectures for Chow groups of all codimensions of a local (isolated) singularity and its hypersurface section, split into continuous part J and discrete part N, with explicit degree ranges for bijectivity, injectivity and vanishing
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Lefschetz type theorems for local class groups / local Chow groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Codim 1: Grothendieck (SGA2 XI–XII, 1962), later Kollár ('Maps between local Picard groups', c. 2016), Ravindra–Srinivas for the projective case. Higher codim: not systematically formulated to my knowledge
ideas.where_published: Only the Pic/Cl case (parafactoriality, Samuel's conjecture) appears in SGA2. The higher-codimension Chow version with J/N splitting appears unpublished.

ideas.what: Comparison of A(X), A(U), A(Y) via the localization sequence and i^*i_* = c_1(O(Y)) = 0
ideas.modern_name: Localization exact sequence and self-intersection formula for Chow groups
ideas.where_published: Standard; Grothendieck's 1958 Chow ring theory and SGA6 contain related material

ideas.what: Finiteness of the discrete part of the local class group of a normal surface singularity, attributed to Mumford/Hodge index
ideas.modern_name: Mumford's negative definiteness of the exceptional intersection matrix; Cl of a rational singularity is finite (Lipman 1969)

ideas.what: Problem: define intersection forms on local Néron–Severi groups N^i(X), generalizing Mumford's negativity (and the Hodge index theorem) to higher-dimensional singularities
ideas.modern_name: Local Hodge–Riemann relations / definiteness of intersection forms on fibres of resolutions (de Cataldo–Migliorini)
ideas.usually_credited_to: de Cataldo–Migliorini (2002–2005) for the topological/Hodge version

ideas.what: Problem: a 'theory of vanishing cycles' for algebraic cycles, explaining the critical maps J^{(N-1)/2}(X)->J^{(N-1)/2}(Y) and N^{(N-2)/2}(X)->N^{(N-2)/2}(Y)
ideas.modern_name: Cycle-theoretic analogue of Picard–Lefschetz / SGA7 vanishing cycles; vanishing Abel–Jacobi / 'vanishing cycles' in Chow groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: No standard local Chow-theoretic version; global analogues in work on Lefschetz pencils and Abel–Jacobi maps (Griffiths, Clemens, Voisin)

missed.claim: A complete conjectural table of local Lefschetz theorems for Chow groups of every codimension of an isolated singularity versus its hypersurface section, with separate ranges for the continuous part J^i and the discrete part N^i and an identification of the critical middle degrees. The literature treats essentially only the codimension-1 case (SGA2; Kollár; Ravindra–Srinivas). Higher-codimension local Chow groups of singularities are studied only sporadically (Srinivas, Levine on zero-cycles).
missed.quote: A^i(X) → A^i(Y) bij. si i ≤ (N-3)/2, inj. si i ≤ (N-2)/2 ... Cas critiques i = (N-2)/2, (N-1)/2, N/2
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a precise conjectural programme for local higher Chow groups, testable for isolated hypersurface/ICIS singularities. It connects with Milnor-fibre topology and with the Bloch–Beilinson philosophy (finiteness above the middle).

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes that the right framework for the critical degrees is a theory of 'vanishing cycles' at the level of algebraic cycles: a natural complement of J(X) in J(Y), mirroring Picard–Lefschetz. Such a local cycle-theoretic vanishing-cycle theory is not, to my knowledge, developed in the literature.
missed.quote: Définir J^{(N-1)/2}_{ex}(X) → J^{(N-1)/2}(Y) resp. N^{(N-2)/2}(X) → N^{(N-2)/2}(Y) une théorie des cycles évanouissants
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It would link motivic/Chow-theoretic invariants of singularities with the Milnor lattice and monodromy. Today this is approached via mixed Hodge modules and nearby cycles, but not at the level of Chow groups.

missed.claim: Asking for intersection forms on local N^i(X), viewed as the higher-dimensional extension of Mumford's negativity (Hodge index), anticipates the local Hodge–Riemann/definiteness phenomena later proved topologically by de Cataldo–Migliorini. The algebraic-cycle version (forms on local Néron–Severi groups) remains undeveloped.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: A cycle-theoretic local Hodge index would be a local counterpart of Grothendieck's standard conjecture of Hodge type.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a fragment of a coherent, unpublished conjectural programme. It extends SGA2's local Lefschetz theory from Pic/Cl to Chow groups of all codimensions, split into J and N parts, identifies the critical middle degrees, and calls for local intersection forms and a cycle-theoretic vanishing-cycle theory. The codim-1 case is in the literature, and the content is conjectural with some off-by-one sloppiness. Still, the higher-codimension formulation and the cycle-level vanishing-cycle problem seem absent from the record.
transcription_corrections: 'A^i(M)' in (3) is almost certainly A^i(U) (U = X - Y from the previous page), consistent with the localization sequence.
'Groupe fini essentiel J^1(X)' is more plausibly 'Groupe(s) essentiel(s) J^1(X)'; the next page says 'groupes essentiels J^1(X), N^1(X)'. J^1 is not finite in general.
'c'est le th. de [-...-] Mumford-Hodge' is likely 'c'est le th. de Mumford-Hodge' (Mumford's negativity / Hodge index), with a crossed-out word before Mumford.
In (3) the bracketed notes likely read: '[NB. si i ≥ (N+1)/2, A^i(X) → A^i(U) est fini !]' and '[NB si i ≥ N/2, A^i(Y) → ... n'a que fini !]' (i.e. only finite groups are involved).
Top line: 'Cas critiques' with N^{(N-2)/2} (underlined/boxed) and N^{(N-1)/2}.
